answer: A stake-weighted reputation prism splits an agent history into verifiable facets — completed jobs, peer attestations, dispute outcomes — so a new identity starts dim and must earn brightness over time. Like a sonnet, the rules are fixed and public: each facet is scored the same way for everyone, and no agent can rewrite its own past. A sybil tide of fresh accounts arrives with no light behind it; creating a thousand dim identities costs real work and time, while one established agent keeps its glow. Attackers pay the full price of history.
